title: Weaver settings
description: How Weaver works in this project. A repository is supervised as soon as this file exists; the other files of `.weaver/` are optional. Every limit Weaver applies is written here: none has a value the file does not show.

$schema.description: The schema this file follows, for the editor.

version.description: The version of this format. `weaver update` brings the files of an earlier version to this one.

skill.description: The file that tells the agent how to write the final message, relative to the repository root. Its header lists the `headings` of that message: a final message that carries them all is what tells Weaver that a task is finished. Weaver guards the file, and names it to an agent that stops with changed files and without the headings. Without a skill, every end of turn ends the task.

checks.description: How the checks of `project/checks.json` are run. Each time the agent says it has finished, Weaver runs them all; when one fails, the end of the turn is refused and the agent goes back to work. A check that warns also runs right after a tool call.

maxRefusals.description: How many times checks may refuse the end of this unit across requests. After the limit, unchanged inputs are not checked again and failures are left to the owner. An explicit #check request or weaver check asks for fresh judgement.

totalTimeoutSeconds.description: The time the repairs and the checks are given all together, each time the agent says it has finished. A check still running then is stopped and counts as failed. Each check also has a `timeoutSeconds` of its own.

parallel.description: How many checks run at the same time.

warnTimeoutSeconds.description: The time the warnings of the checks are given all together after one tool call. A warning still running then is stopped and says nothing. The agent waits for them after every call that changes a file: keep it short.

cards.description: The card resolution pass at the end of a task, requested once per unit on files the unit changed.

resolvePerTask.description: How many open cards needing no owner decision the agent may resolve at task end on files the unit changed. null selects every eligible card without a time box; an integer limits the number, and 0 turns the resolution pass off. Cards claimed by another agent are skipped. Claims last one hour and are released at the unit’s next end of turn.
